name: list_projects
title: List projects
description: Projects the caller can read, by slug. Every other tool takes a project slug.

name: get_protocol
title: Get the working protocol
description: The whole working protocol, docs/agents.md, as Markdown, with its version, sha256 and size (GET /api/protocol), and base_url, the server's base URL its REST paths start at: every REST request, a download_url included, carries the same Authorization: Bearer header as MCP. Read it before you start: the server's instructions are only its opening. Every claim and job claim names it as protocol with its sha256; read it again when the digest differs from the copy you read.

name: list_schemas
title: List the contract schemas
description: The name, reference and a one-line description of every published contract schema: the documents the tools take (unit and its acceptance, artifact_manifest, run, verification, writeup, decision, concern, transcript, brief, track, job_completion, job_failure, ...). Read one with get_schema.

name: get_schema
title: Get a contract schema
description: A published contract schema by name, as one self-contained JSON Schema (GET /api/schemas/{name}): required keys, types, patterns, enums and descriptions. unit holds a plan unit's fields and its acceptance; artifact_manifest what post_manifest records; run, verification, writeup, decision, concern and brief the front matter of those documents (a write-up you write is writeup's first variant, "Write-up"; "Imported write-up" is for imports only); transcript one transcript event. Validate a document against it before you send it.

name.description: The schema's name, as list_schemas lists it.
name.title: Name

name: get_brief

name: revise_brief

name: start_plan_revision
title: Start a plan revision
description: Open the next revision of a track's plan as a draft (researchers; acting for one, you are recorded as the channel). A revision starts from the approved plan, or from a newer revision sent back: its approach, its new units and its units still queued. needs_alignment lists the done and in-flight units the revision must say something about with set_alignment, and needs_answer the open concerns it answers with answer_concern. One open revision per track.

name: get_plan
title: Get a track's plan
description: One revision of a track's plan: its approach, its units with their acceptance, parameters, relations, context and brief, its alignment entries and its review. revision is a number, "draft" (the open revision) or "current" (the approved plan, else the newest revision; the default). A track with no plan revision yet answers not_found: start its first revision with start_plan_revision. A unit the plan adds has number null until the plan is approved; approval assigns the numbers, and list_track_units then lists them.

revision.description: A revision number, draft or current; omitted, current.

name: set_plan_approach

name: add_unit
title: Add a unit to the plan
description: Add a unit of work to the draft. acceptance is how the result is judged (get_schema unit gives the whole shape): selection_splits and confirmation_splits (split slugs, as metric_catalog lists them), primary_metric (a metric key), required_slices (dimension names only, such as ["language"]: every value of each named dimension must be reported; metric_catalog lists each metric's dimensions and their values), success_criteria and falsification_criteria (text), regression_gates (dimension names or policy gate ids) and compute_budget (an object of upper bounds, each a non-negative number named <resource>_max; the conventional names are gpu_hours_max, cpu_hours_max, wall_clock_hours_max and cost_usd_max, such as {"gpu_hours_max": 4, "wall_clock_hours_max": 2}, and any other snake-case <resource>_max is accepted), all required, checked against the project's metric registry. parameters are the project's unit fields. relations name another unit with a kind: derived_from, supersedes or related_to. context lists what its performer should read: {kind: unit, unit: number or key}, {kind: writeup, unit: number, attempt: sequence} or {kind: artifact, artifact: id}, each with an optional note. brief is the unit's own Markdown for whoever runs it. The unit has no number until a researcher approves the plan: get_plan shows it with number null until then, and other units of the plan name it by its key. Refused over the project's limits (unit brief 32 KiB, 64 context items by default); a refusal names each failing field and what it expected.

Approval assigns each new unit its number.

The document is Markdown with YAML front matter (GET /api/schemas/concern): kind (wrong_assumption, better_idea, blocker or other) and, when it comes from one, the unit number and attempt sequence; the argument as the body (at most 16 KiB). While it is open no new unit of the track can be claimed; work already claimed continues. A plan revision answers it, or a researcher dismisses it. Do not raise one for a problem with your own run: release the attempt with a failure report instead.

name: claim_unit
title: Claim a queued unit
description: Claim a queued unit (a given number, or the next one, optionally in a track) and receive an attempt with a lease token and generation. Heartbeat before the lease expires. Agents and researchers claim only units of `agent`-mode tracks; `workflow` tracks are claimed only by an experimenter (a Cannery Row runner). The claim's context names the attempt's context bundle: call the tool it names (context.tool, get_context) with context.arguments, or read the MCP resource context.resource. Read it first: its Submitting section says what the run must submit.

mode.description: Claim only in tracks of this mode. Only an `experimenter` service account (a Cannery Row runner) claims in `workflow` mode, and only there; agents and researchers claim in `agent` mode. Omitted, the caller's mode applies.

name: get_context
title: Get an attempt's context bundle
description: The context bundle of an attempt, as Markdown (GET /api/projects/{slug}/units/{number}/attempts/{sequence}/context.md). Read it first: the brief, the plan's approach, the unit's fields, acceptance and brief, a section Submitting that says what the run must submit (the required artifact roles, the metrics with their keys, directions and slices, the datasets and splits, the interfaces, how to build the manifest, with an example, and the run document's front matter), the track's other units, the context items, and what earlier attempts asked, were told and why they failed. A claim (claim_unit) names the exact call as context.tool and context.arguments; so does a job claim (claim_job), whose bundle is the attempt's with phase verify, document or decide for a verify, document or decide job. detail compact keeps the brief's goal, the unit, Submitting and the index, under 16 KiB.

sequence.title: Sequence

phase.description: verify: the verifier's bundle, which replaces Submitting with what the verifier produces (its steps, the required output roles and each field of the verification report with the values it must name, and an example completion); document: the documenter's bundle, which adds every attempt's run document and notes, failures and their logs, verification reports and comments; decide: the decider's, which adds the write-up and the exact verification and writeup a decision cites. Omitted: the performer's bundle.

name: claim_job
title: Claim a job
description: Claim the oldest waiting job of a phase the caller may perform. verify (the default): a verifier service account receives jobs whose science revision has the runner perform verify and names it; an agent service account or a researcher receives jobs whose verify performer is agent, never of an attempt it ran itself. document: an agent service account or a researcher receives the oldest unit waiting for its write-up. decide: the decider service account a science revision registers receives the oldest unit waiting for its automatic decision. The job document carries its lease token once. Its context names the job's context bundle: call context.tool (get_context) with context.arguments (phase verify, document or decide). Its output says what complete_job takes: the document's contract (verification, writeup or decision), whether a manifest goes with it, the artifact roles the manifest must list with what each holds, and for a verify job the values the report must name (policy, science, source and control revisions and the dataset revisions it may name). A verify job's inputs are read with get_job_input: run, manifest and artifacts.

name: complete_job
title: Complete a job
description:
Complete the claimed job. document is {"schema_version": "0.2", "job_id": "<the job's id>", "document": "<Markdown with YAML front matter>"}, plus "manifest" for a verify job; the job claim's output says which contract the document follows, whether a manifest goes with it, the artifact roles that manifest must list (output.required_roles) and, for a verify job, the values the report must name (output.expected). A verify job: the verification report (get_schema verification) and the manifest of what the job uploaded (get_schema artifact_manifest), listing every required output role; only the uploads the manifest lists are the job's outputs. Its policy_revision is output.expected.policy_revision (an agent verifier's is the pinned science revision), its provenance names output.expected's science, source and control revisions (the control's bare revision, such as "r1") and one of its dataset_revisions; the verifier's context bundle (get_context with phase verify) has a worked example. A document job: the write-up (get_schema writeup), in the schema's first variant, "Write-up" (never "Imported write-up", which only imports use), and no manifest, for example "---
summary: One sentence the unit page opens with.
attempts: [1, 2]
verification:
  ref: <the job's inputs.verification.ref>
  sha256: <its sha256>
---
What was tried, what was found and what it means.
": attempts lists every attempt of the unit, and verification is the job's inputs.verification, null for a stopped unit. A decide job: the decision document (get_schema decision) citing the verification report and write-up the job inputs name, and no manifest; it promotes only on a pass verdict. An invalid document from an agent, a researcher or a decider is refused with the details (a manifest without a required role names missing_roles and required_roles) and the lease is kept; a verifier runner's invalid report fails the job run.

A failed document job is queued again.

name: record_decision
title: Record a human decision
description: Record a researcher's decision on a pending review case (list_review_cases, get_review_case); the case's kind says which fields to send. A decision case (kind decision) takes document only: the decision document, Markdown with YAML front matter (get_schema decision) naming the outcome (promote, reject, inconclusive, or failed for a unit stopped after a failure) and citing the case's verification report and write-up, the reason as its body; supersedes corrects an earlier decision, including one a decider recorded. While a decide job of a registered decider waits or runs, the case is its to decide. A failure case (kind failure) takes action (retry or stop), evidence_revision (the case's subject_revision: the failure revision decided on) and reason, and no document. Only people with the researcher role may; service account tokens are refused.

name: write_up
title: Write a unit up
description:
A researcher writes a unit up in one action, claiming and completing its document job: Markdown with YAML front matter (GET /api/schemas/writeup) with a one-sentence summary, the attempts it covers and the verification report it cites, as get_writeup names them, and a body. An agent claims the document job instead (claim_job with phase document). document is the write-up itself, a string, in the writeup schema's first variant, "Write-up" (never "Imported write-up", which only imports use), for example "---
summary: One sentence the unit page opens with.
attempts: [1, 2]
verification:
  ref: <get_writeup's inputs.verification.ref>
  sha256: <its sha256>
---
What was tried, what was found and what it means.
": attempts lists every attempt of the unit, verification is null for a unit stopped after a failure, and the body is not empty.

name: ask
title: Ask a question about your unit
description: Ask a researcher a question about the unit under your attempt's lease (agent mode). body is your question as Markdown. A blocking question stops your lease clock until it is answered: wait with wait_for_answer or keep heartbeating, and do nothing else on the attempt meanwhile. A non-blocking question states the default you proceed on until it is answered (default is required). Returns the question message: its id (pass it to wait_for_answer), kind question, body, blocking, default and state; its question field is null, since that field is set only on an answer, naming the question it answers. Raise a concern instead when the track's plan itself is wrong.

name: list_questions
title: List questions
description: The questions performers asked about the project's units, newest first, with their answers: of one track when track is given, in one state when state is given (open ones wait for a researcher). A question's text is its body, and its answer, once given, is answer (null until then), whose text is answer.body. The question field is always null on a question: it is set only on the answer messages list_messages returns, where it names the question answered.

name: get_question
title: Read a question
description: One question: who asked it, under which attempt or job, whether it blocks, the default it proceeds on, and its answer once given. A question's text is its body, and its answer, once given, is answer (null until then), whose text is answer.body. The question field is always null on a question: it is set only on the answer messages list_messages returns, where it names the question answered.

name: wait_for_answer
title: Wait for an answer
description: Long-poll for the answer to a question: wait up to wait seconds (default 20, at most 25, under common MCP client timeouts) for it to be answered or escalated, then return it with its answer, or with answer null when the wait ran out. Call it again in a loop until answer is set or state is no longer open; keep heartbeating a non-blocking question's attempt meanwhile. An answer to your own question is acknowledged as it is returned: no ack_steering needed for it.

wait.description: Seconds to wait for the answer.
wait.title: Wait

name: answer_question
title: Answer a question
description: Answer an open question, as Markdown (researchers). The performer reads it with wait_for_answer or in its next heartbeat; a blocking question's attempt or job gets a fresh lease and runs on. An answer replies to that question only; an unasked note to a running attempt is a steering note (post_steering).

name: escalate_question
title: Escalate a question into a concern
description: Turn an open question into a concern about the plan of its unit's track (researchers): the concern takes the kind and the note and quotes the question, and blocks new claims on the track until a plan revision answers it or it is dismissed. The note answers the question.

description: Acknowledge by id the steering notes and the answers you have read, once you act on them: heartbeat responses stop carrying them and the researcher sees you took them in. An answer that wait_for_answer returned to you is already acknowledged. Returns acknowledged, every id you sent, all now acknowledged, and already_acknowledged, those that were before this call (by wait_for_answer or an earlier ack); acknowledging twice is harmless.

Submitting the attempt seals the transcript; an append over the project's transcript_max_bytes is refused with its size and the limit. ts is optional: the server stamps each event with received_at as it is appended, so leave ts out rather than guess a time.
